⚠
Untagged is largely recoverable. Of the ~4,490 "direct/untagged" module views, only 1,604 (36%) are genuinely untagged. The rest carry a page signal: 1,194 from the coins/explore page, 1,155 from paid advertising (external acquisition landing in Experiences — previously invisible), and 628 from the home page without a type tag. The deeplink, widget_id and page_id fields are 100% empty on every untagged row, so page is the only recovery lever — a clean fix would be to have the app always stamp source_attribute_type, not just source_attribute_page.
🔍
What the 1,604 truly-untagged users actually did (raw-event probe): they're not mysterious — traced through the raw timestamped log, the event firing immediately before their untagged entry is dynamic_link_executed for 704 of them (a deep link — shared link, notification, or external URL), plus 517 cold-booting straight into scapia_experiences_initialised, 109 via a home category CTA, and 81 via the home icon itself. Root cause: when Experiences opens from a deep-link cold-start, the app doesn't stamp source_attribute_type on the TEA event. So "untagged" ≈ "deep-link entry." Business impact is tiny (the untagged-everywhere core produced 1 booking / ₹12.6k in August), but the fix is clear: propagate the deep-link source into the TEA attribution context.

Home page icon dominates (~46% of tagged views). The recovered paid advertising stream (1,155 users) is a genuine new insight — it was hidden in the untagged bucket and shows external spend is driving Experiences entries that weren't being credited. Coins page (1,194) confirms the carousel is a real entry channel.

Median return gap is 3 days (avg 4.8). Nearly 1 in 5 users come back after leaving — and 2,931 re-open product pages on a different day, meaning they're actively deliberating, not lost. This is the exact audience a retargeting push/WhatsApp should hit: a user who viewed a PDP and left has a 2–7 day consideration window. A "still thinking about [city]?" nudge timed to day 2–3 is squarely aligned with observed behaviour. Where the time actually goes: users reach a PDP fast (median 45s from entry) and spend only ~16s on it — they're either quickly convinced or they bounce, so the PDP isn't where hesitation lives. The real friction is Variant → checkout submit at 4.0 minutes — the traveller-details / date-and-slot form is by far the slowest step, ~15× longer than any other. That's the screen to simplify (pre-fill traveller info, fewer required fields) to compress the 38-minute end-to-end path. Payment itself is instant (3s submit→pay), so checkout mechanics aren't the problem — the form is.

11 · Merchandising — placement impact (entering → orders → GMV, by hosting screen)

"Hosted on" is derived directly from a live join against source_attribute_type/source_attribute_page in simple.crud.percept_event_agg (run this session) — where a tag's underlying page varies, the split observed in that join is stated rather than picking one. The raw tag itself is shown as-is (Scapia owns the naming convention for the segment-prefixed codes nu_/ta_/tina_/th_/sp_/fp_/cp_), never guessed at. Orders/GMV here use entry-date attribution — every order ever placed by a user who entered via that placement in the selected window, however long after entry the order actually closed — rather than the booking-date filter used in every other Orders/GMV column in this dashboard (there, "orders in the selected range" means bookings that closed in that range). This is a deliberate, different, and equally valid cut (it answers "how much did this placement's entrants eventually spend," not "how much closed this week"), but the two will not sum to identical totals for the same date range and should not be compared cell-for-cell against Section 2/3/12 — a small persistent gap (roughly ~2% of orders and ~1% of GMV, all-time) is expected and comes from exactly this different date basis, not from an error.

19 · Deep-link sources & the CRM routing bug — raw-event evidence (P0)

You asked whether the untagged deep-link entries are actually your CRM links (push / WhatsApp / email). The raw log confirms it: every dynamic_link_executed event carries a dynamic_link_source and a dynamic_link_type (destination). Aug 16, app-wide.

Aug 15 slot-PN test — did the deep-link get fixed?
No, not for CRM/Push broadcasts. The Aug 15 Independence-Day slot PN (3 push campaigns: 41,273 sent, 164 clicks, 243 TEA entries) produced 0 bookings — its Branch deep-links still resolved to tea/home (CRM → tea/home: 243, Push → tea/home: 26), not the city or product page. MoEngage's own conversion attribution agrees — Goal 1 (tea_order_updates COMPLETE) = 0 bookings, ₹0 revenue; so both DB and MoEngage independently show zero conversions.
What HAS started working: in-app merch deep-links now route correctly — merch → tea/collection (160), tea/city-srp (129), tea/product-family (58), tea/product-details (57). So the routing fix landed for merchandising placements, but not for CRM push / WhatsApp / broadcast links. The P0 is still open for CRM.

Yes — CRM, Push, WhatsApp, CRM-PN, PN and Email all generate deep links (~4,864 users/day combined). So the untagged Experiences entries genuinely include your CRM traffic; the app just fails to stamp the source onto the TEA event.

🔴
The routing bug, proven end-to-end. Of the CRM/Push/WhatsApp deep links that are meant for Experiences on Aug 16, the destination is almost always tea/home — the generic landing — not a city or product page: Push→tea/home (33), CRM→tea/home (10), WhatsApp→tea/home (6), vs merch links which correctly target tea/city-srp, tea/collection and tea/product-details. Then tracing those 54 CRM-TEA deep-link users forward: 29 (54%) hit the mpin blocker screen, only 28 reached the TEA module, just 4 reached a city page and 12 a PDP. This is the P0 you flagged from MoEngage, now confirmed in the app's own event stream: CRM links point at the Experiences home (not the specific city/product), and the mpin auth interrupts half of them before they arrive.

Two fixes, both on the app/CRM side: (1) construct CRM deep links to target the specific tea/city-srp or tea/product-details for the campaign, not the generic tea/home; (2) persist the deep-link destination across the mpin screen so auth doesn't drop the user on the home page. Until both ship, CRM's Experiences pushes can't convert regardless of copy or targeting.

21 · Methodology & data-quality notes — read before presenting

Two different dates are used, on purpose, never mixed within one number: Entering/Browse/Product/Checkout columns are keyed by entry date (when the user's TEA journey started). Orders/GMV columns are keyed by booking date (when the order was actually placed), attributed back to that user's original entry bucket. Column headers say which. Booking date is used for orders because a user who enters on a given day usually books days later — showing orders by entry date instead makes any recent single day look almost empty even when actual bookings that day were normal, which is why the previous version undercounted "yesterday's" bookings.

Source tables: simple.crud.percept_event_agg (daily aggregated TEA events, source of the entry/funnel cube), rds_main.scapiadb.orders (bookings, filtered to product_category='EXPERIENCE' and status='COMPLETE'), simple.crud.crm_campaign_content joined on campaign_name = source_attribute_id (the join key that actually works — campaign_id in that table is an internal MoEngage object id, not the human-readable name used elsewhere), simple.crud.user_location and simple.crud.event_location_agg (in-trip/pre-trip signals, both fresh through 2026-08-11; the sibling table percept_location_agg is stale since 2026-07-09 and was not used).

Entry-window: full available history, 2025-10-16 to 2026-08-11 (300 days). The first week of tracking (Oct 16–23, 2025) contains an anomalous single-day spike consistent with a backfill/test burst — left in for transparency, flagged here rather than silently removed.

Booking traceability: 4,035 of 4,058 total completed Experience orders (99.4%) are traced to a specific entry bucket and date. Of the 2,883 distinct users who ever completed an Experience booking, 8 (0.28%) have no TEA funnel event anywhere in the tracked history — most likely booked through a channel this event set doesn't instrument (e.g. web/CX-assisted checkout) or under a different user id than the one that browsed.

Excluded as junk: a small number of source_attribute_type values (each appearing exactly once, all-time) are SQL-injection / SSRF security-probe payloads against the tracking endpoint, not real user activity. They are excluded from every bucket above rather than silently folded into "Unattributed".

"Unattributed" (formerly labelled "Organic/Direct"): renamed because the old label overstated what's known. It means the attribution field was empty AND the deeplink/page_id/widget_id trace fields were also empty, checked directly — not that no interaction occurred. See section 7 for the breakdown of which screen these users actually land on first.

Funnel level definitions: Browse = module/city/collection/family/autosuggest view, Product = PDP view, Checkout Started (tea_checkout_start) = opened the booking/checkout flow for a specific product, Checkout Submitted (tea_checkout_detail_submit) = submitted the booking details form (traveler/slot/variant info) within that flow, Booked = order marked COMPLETE (paid) in the orders table. Checkout Submitted sits between Checkout Started and Booked — verified from live counts (Checkout Started 940 distinct users in the last 14 days vs. Checkout Submitted 340 in the same window, consistent with it being the narrower, later step), not from any event dictionary, since none exists for this event in the tables checked. Mixpanel separately tracks a tea_payments event between submit and booking, but that event is not present in the Databricks table this dashboard reads from, so it isn't shown here. Each level is "reached this deep or deeper" (cumulative), so the funnel is monotonic regardless of the order any individual user actually clicked through.

Known gap, stated plainly: no WhatsApp/Push send-or-delivery log table exists anywhere in simple.crud (checked exhaustively) — campaign performance below is entrants-who-engaged only, not send→deliver→click funnels, because that data does not exist in this warehouse.

Which sections respond to the controls above: KPIs, entry attribution, funnel tree, trend, time-between-stages (averages), merchandising placement impact, unattributed breakdown, campaigns, booking cities, in-trip country table, and AOV/day-of-week all recompute from the selected date range. Three things do not, by the nature of the underlying metric, and each says so in its own section: (1) time-between-stage medians cannot be validly recombined from per-day medians, so the median column stays all-time even though the average column is range-aware; (2) pre-trip search→TEA-entry conversion is a 14-day-forward-looking cohort metric — slicing it to an arbitrary end date would silently truncate the forward window for the most recent cohorts and understate conversion, so it is kept on its own fixed rolling window; (3) the Mixpanel cross-check is a single fixed-day spot check by design (it exists to confirm the two systems agree on one day, not to be a live comparison tool). In-trip's channel and top-cities cuts remain all-time supplementary detail (noted inline) because they were not re-pulled at daily grain this round — the country table, which was the specific ask, is fully date-aware.

This is a custom Mixpanel event that fires at booking confirmation. Our DB (sections 1–12 above) showed 21 because the data was queried on Aug 12 while orders were still settling. The live Databricks dashboard (Section 16 below, fetched Aug 14) confirms 42 total bookings, 34 distinct bookers on Aug 12 — exactly matching Mixpanel's TEA Booking Done = 34 unique users.
